clusters.pick_reason: #2514 implements the complete spec-compliant solution — it adds the `CancelledNotificationParams` import needed to actually emit `notifications/cancelled` per the MCP spec, and removes the stray `# pragma: no cover` suggesting it brings the code path under test. #2493 only removes the wrong error-response send without providing the spec-required replacement notification, leaving cancellation behavior incomplete. #2514 subsumes #2493's change and delivers the full fix.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both PRs fix the same incorrect behavior in `RequestResponder.cancel()` in `session.py`: the method was sending an error response on cancellation, which violates the MCP spec. #2493 removes the erroneous error-response send and makes `server.py` return without sending any response for cancelled requests. #2514 goes further by adding `CancelledNotificationParams` (the import is visible in the diff) to send the spec-required `notifications/cancelled` message instead. They modify the same method body and are two halves of the same fix: remove the wrong behavior, add the correct one.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2777 follows the more idiomatic Python pattern: when chaining with `from e`, the original exception is already accessible via `__cause__` in the traceback, so embedding `{e}` in the message string is redundant. Removing it (as #2777 does) produces cleaner, non-duplicated error messages (`OAuthRegistrationError: Invalid registration response` with the `ValidationError` attached as cause) rather than the double-reporting in #2565 (`OAuthRegistrationError: Invalid registration response: <ValidationError text>` plus the same `ValidationError` as `__cause__`).

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2730 additionally imports base64, indicating it encodes header values rather than sending raw strings — matching the SEP-2243 spec requirement for encoded method/name fields. PR #2724 adds the same constants and signature change but lacks the encoding step, so its headers would be malformed for non-ASCII method names.
